questions: Is the inversion number defined as the count of pairs (i, j) such that i < j and B_i > B_j, or i < j and B_i >= B_j?
Should the output lines correspond to k values from 0 to M-1 in ascending order, or in the order of some other sequence?
Are there any constraints on the sum of N and M, or is the 2e5 limit per variable individually?
If M=1, all remainders are 0; is the inversion number then 0, or should it be computed normally (which would also be 0)?
Should the solution handle cases where N*M is large (up to 4e10) in terms of time complexity, or is an O(M log M) or O(N log N) solution expected?
Is the input sequence A guaranteed to be non-empty (N >= 1), and if N=1, is the inversion number always 0?
Do we need to consider integer overflow in inversion counts, and if so, should output be modulo something?
For the inversion count, are duplicate values in B considered inversions? (i.e., if B_i = B_j for i < j, does it count?)
